policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the priests sounded with the trumpets' renders either spelling of the hiphil participle of חצר; qere מַחְצְרִים and ketiv מחצצרים differ only orthographically and no ASV note is mapped to this unit. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
ASV text reads 'Ephron', the ketiv עפרון; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, Ephrain' names the qere עֶפְרַיִן as the reading not adopted.
